header.name: Introduction to free non commutative function theory
header.description: This course provides an introduction to free noncommutative (nc) function theory, a modern branch of analysis at the intersection of operator theory, complex analysis, and noncommutative geometry. It covers the foundations of nc sets and nc functions, nc difference-differential calculus, Taylor–Taylor expansions, topologies on nc spaces, and notions of nc analyticity. The course further introduces higher-order nc functions and concludes with the theory of free noncommutative reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. Emphasis is placed on both the theoretical foundations and their applications to contemporary research in free analysis and operator theory.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to demonstrate understanding of the theory of free noncommutative sets, functions and their algebraic properties.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to define the analyticity in the category of free noncommutative functions, explain their elementary properties and utilise them in their research work.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will develop knowledge on the higher order noncommutative functions.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to define the free noncommutative reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces consisting of noncommutative functions.

lecture_topics: Notion of nc sets, functions and their elementary properties with a number of examples.
Topologies on nc spaces and nc sets
Higher order nc functions and their analyticy, specially for 1 order nc functions.
Free noncommutative reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces of nc functions and their elementary properties.
